task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0020 -- design the fix for the S10 blocked-user notification gap present at BOTH notification sites in apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts (makeStaffAddHandler and makeStaffRemoveHandler), per ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: Design covers both call sites (assignment and removal), not just the one ISS-0020 originally named
getUserByTgUsername's projection change specified exactly, with no-other-caller verification

Skip-check logic at both sites specified precisely (guard-clause shape, no new control flow beyond it), matching sendLedgeredNotification's skip semantics rather than the now-removed withdraw.ts inline guard
Open question (organizer-facing surfacing of a blocked-skip) explicitly resolved with reasoning, not silently assumed
REQ-023.md §6.2's now-doubly-inaccurate claim noted as a correction in the new artefact, without editing REQ-023.md itself
No implementation code (design doc contains no .ts/.tsx code blocks with real logic -- signatures, interfaces, and a prose rule table only)
Scope held to the minimal fix -- no ledger routing, no staff.ts refactor beyond the two call sites and one lookup function

result.summary: Wrote docs/agents/design/ISS-0020-fix.md. Verified ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis independently: confirmed both staff.ts sites (lines 98, 168) lack a blocked check, confirmed getUserByTgUsername (domain/user.ts lines 132-142) has exactly one caller file (staff.ts, both handlers) via grep, so widening its UserWithTelegram return interface to add `blocked: boolean` (projecting users.blocked) is purely additive and safe. Confirmed withdraw.ts's inline guard no longer exists (REQ-025 replaced it with sendLedgeredNotification) and confirmed sendLedgeredNotification is structurally unavailable to staff.ts (registrationId NOT NULL FK, closed NotificationKind union with no staff-assignment member) -- ledger routing correctly excluded from scope. Design: getUserByTgUsername's signature is unchanged; only its returned UserWithTelegram interface gains `blocked`. At both call sites, a guard clause skips entering the existing try{...ctx.api.sendMessage...} block when targetUser.blocked is true, and reuses the SAME existing notificationFailed flag (no new variable/branch) -- treating a blocked-skip identically to the pre-existing thrown-send-failure path. RESOLVED the organizer-surfacing open question: surface it via the existing notificationFailedNote reply-suffix (reusing the same string, no new catalog key), reasoning that staff.ts's synchronous organizer-initiated command context differs materially from sendLedgeredNotification's passive scheduled-job callers, and reusing the existing generic message avoids leaking the specific 'this person blocked us' distinction while still telling the organizer the send didn't land. Noted REQ-023.md §6.2's now-doubly-inaccurate precedent claim in the new artefact §0 without editing REQ-023.md (out of scope, per task instruction). No implementation code written -- only interface/signature snippets and a prose rule table for the skip-check logic.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for design gate
